method.continuationOwnership: js_backend.code emits code function then conts(body,ctx) before next code; verified source anchors bend2/selfhost/js_backend.bend:847-856 and 1386-1392. Only named declarations and their emitted continuations are joined through the same-line $D sidecar.
method.cpu: Unweighted V8 CPU sample counts for both roles; nearest source provider present on a sampled synchronous stack. One recorded negative interval makes duration-weighted attribution unsuitable; no interval is clamped and no sample is dropped. Unkeyed code and CPS-erased ancestry stay unassigned.
method.allocation: Sum sampled selfSize once per allocation tree node; nearest source provider on the retained allocation stack. Not exact allocated bytes or retained memory.
method.chunks: Pending request constructor at 64-step boundaries; not durations, per-definition calls or precise stage boundaries.

moduleResidency.policy: One actual image instance for parse/expand/check/emit; no per-stage, per-role or per-lane module alias.

cpu.weighting: Unweighted sample counts in both roles; no sample dropped or interval clamped. Original timeDeltas retained in raw profiles; candidate has a negative interval, so duration-weighted attribution is not used.

chunkAttribution.reason: Request-group wrappers were not unwrapped by the diagnostic observer; pending provider counts cannot be recovered from its aggregate. CPU/allocation source ownership is analyzed separately.

observed.clock: host chunk boundaries of the emit Run; counts only, never durations
observed.limitation: A tag is the pending constructor after a 64-step chunk; it names a composed-source definition on the chunk, not proof that the private transform ran and not a duration.

attribution.method: emit-profile.mjs static text scan: /^function (\$bN)\(/ for code ids; the first $bN inside each $D["<key>"]= assignment segment (bounded 2000 chars) is that declaration's entry code. No disassembly, no heap snapshot, no execution.
attribution.limitation: Only $D-declared entry codes are keyed. Nested lambdas and transform-created worker bodies have no declared key in the image and stay unmapped rather than being guessed; join CPU-profile functionName "$bN" through the sidecar map.

reference.direction: absentFromReference means "this unkeyed code id does not exist in the supplied reference image"; aboveReferenceMaxUnkeyed is the subset above the reference maximum code id. Absence is NOT proof of transform-created bodies: a regenerated step module can add keyed definitions whose private bodies land here. Only the census counters attest the vector workers. Text scan only; the reference is never imported or executed.

sourcePreservationIncident.scope: Temporary diagnostic script path only; no image, frozen source, helper or request was changed.
sourcePreservationIncident.cause: Delegated author applied follow-up driver validation edits after parent launched the pinned original module. Parent stopped further edits and restored the loaded source bytes before original post-run pin check and before the second serial role starts.
sourcePreservationIncident.qualification: Accept diagnostic only if both role reports record original own driver hash, all pins pass, both exact expected output hashes match and guardians PASS. Otherwise retain failed run and rerun fresh; never suppress a pin failure.

limitations: Both roles ran the original unmodified images with exactly one imported module; the original driver source was restored byte-exact before post-run pin checks and the second serial role.
The pending-request histogram is unusable: it did not unwrap request-group constructors. No provider counts from that histogram are used.
Role-specific provider numbering is required: js_backend is provider 8 in R12 and 9 in G32. Corrected CPU/allocation attribution uses each role's authenticated composition order.
79-80% of CPU samples remain unattributed by synchronous source-stack ownership. Complete logical intervals are measured separately, not fabricated from those samples.
One candidate CPU timeDelta is -42 microseconds. Both roles use all unweighted samples; no negative value is clamped and no sample is dropped.
Sampled allocation selfSize estimates are neither exact allocated bytes nor retained heap; profiler timing is not unprofiled acceptance.
